speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will provide greater granularity in reporting employment outcomes of adult learning programmes such as the SkillsFuture Career Transition and Work-Study Programmes including the provision of sectoral breakdowns in growth areas like artificial intelligence, healthcare and social services, so as to assess the effectiveness of these programmes more clearly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Employment outcomes, including wage changes and placement rates provide a quantitative measure on the impact of learning, including the industry relevance of skills training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Today, we track and report employment outcomes via administrative data, programme-specific surveys and econometric studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Every year, the polytechnics and ITE also administer the Work-Study Programme Outcomes Survey to work-study graduates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We will review the Member's suggestion on how better to report employment outcomes to guide individuals' training decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Where the studies are conclusive, such as the MTI's econometric studies, we have published them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Some programmes also equip learners with horizontal skills, such as data analytics and artificial intelligence-related skills, that can be applied to job roles across multiple sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Further, wage and employment outcomes do not tell us the full picture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: For example, reskilling could have helped workers, who are at risk of displacement, keep their jobs, or take on new job roles in a growth sector, albeit with an initial pay cut.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Some workers might also learn new skills in anticipation of new or upcoming requirements, for example, an automotive mechanic learning how to maintain electric vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In such cases, wage effects may be hard to quantify.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Therefore, MOE and SSG take a broader view of the impact of the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: To complement the employment outcomes reporting, SSG administers the Training Quality and Outcomes Measure (TRAQOM) survey to learners who take up SSG-funded programmes to rate the programme quality and perceived outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This includes whether the training has helped them to be more effective at their jobs, improve their work performance or allow them to take on enhanced responsibilities at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The TRAQOM ratings of each course are published on MySkillsFuture portal and guide learners on suitable training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Other than employment outcomes, SSG also studies job posting data to monitor how job roles and skills needs of the labour market are evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Such jobs-skills insights are published regularly to inform the training market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: For example, SSG's annual Skills Demand for the Future Economy report highlights changes to the in-demand skills in the digital, care and green economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: SSG also makes available jobs-skills tools and resources under the Jobs-Skills Portal to help companies and training providers focus on building up relevant skills for their workers and trainees.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Minister of State for the detailed reply.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I am coming from an angle of providing information in terms of sectors so that both learners and employers can then know which sectors actually provide better career transitions.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: So, I am wondering if the Ministry will be able to look at, perhaps, for the sectors that have higher sample sizes, what the outcomes are, in terms of the current matrices that the Ministry is already tracking and publishing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we will continue to study the variety of means through which we can help the learners, the employers and also the training providers make the correct choices, in terms of the courses that the learners select to go on, creating opportunities, the opportunities created by employers, and the training providers that need to then develop capacity in order to then provide the training for the learners.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we do need to make this information available.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As I have explained, the outcomes are not so simple because some of them are distant in the future, some of them are stackable on top of each other.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we have to track all of these and think through how we can best provide the information; and how we can then guide the learners and the workers as well as the employers and the training providers, in order to think of the future capacity and the future opportunity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As I have explained, we have to think about wage outcomes and job placements but also job roles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And some of it is also a consideration of then what would have happened, the counterfactual, the worker who was not displaced but stayed in the job role or transited to another domain and potentially took a pay cut, but that was the counterfactual to losing the job entirely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have to think through how we present the data in a way that informs learners, employers and training providers in helping them make decisions about SkillsFuture's future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was trying to squeeze in one more Parliamentary Question (PQ), but time is up.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I ask for Members' indulgence and understanding.
